claims.statement: The organization's settings sidebar under Code, planning, and automation leads through Repository to Custom properties. The included code-planning-automation fragment was read in full. The screenshot caption identifies the outlined link only; no image inspection, property inventory, setting state, or permissions were verified.

The add-domain control sits beside a heading referring to verified and approved domains for an enterprise account, despite this fragment's organizations directory. Navigation is not proof of domain verification, approval, ownership, or organization-only scope.

The containing DNS-verification procedure directs creation of a DNS TXT record with the domain host using the displayed instructions. No record name, value, TTL, authority, propagation result, ownership decision, or successful verification is supplied by this fragment; no DNS mutation was performed.

The intended domain is entered and submitted through Add domain. Submission is distinct from successful DNS verification or approval; the fragment specifies neither a concrete domain nor mutation authorization.

Each issued client certificate must identify its GitHub user through an extension. The linked pinned SSH-CA guide's issuing context was inspected: identity validation precedes issuance, login identification is described with conditionally available user-ID support, and hostname/product contexts matter. Already-issued individual certificates cannot be revoked while their issuing CA remains trusted; removing CA trust invalidates all its signed certificates. This dependency inspection is not whole-page review, full conditional resolution, certificate issuance, trusted-CA configuration, or proof of effective access.

During the containing user-addition flow, choosing an organization team is optional. Selecting a team is not independently verified membership, invitation acceptance, permission inheritance, or authorization to add anyone.
